sentences: I rinse glass jars and metal cans before placing them in the blue recycling bin by the curb.
I check the numbered triangle on plastic containers to decide whether the local program accepts them.
I flatten cardboard boxes and stack them beside the paper bin so they take up less space.
I separate newspapers, magazines, and office paper into a marked bin for the weekly collection truck.
I remove plastic caps from bottles and put the caps in a separate container for drop-off.
I empty and rinse aluminum cans, then crush them before adding them to the recycling bag.
I keep a small bin in the kitchen for food scraps that go to the municipal compost program.
I take used batteries to a designated collection box at the hardware store instead of the trash.
I place broken electronics in a cardboard box and drive them to the county e-waste drop-off site.
I check the recycling guide posted on the fridge before I sort any item from the bathroom.
I scrape food residue from plastic tubs into the sink and then place the tubs in the recycling bin.
I bundle clean plastic bags at the grocery store collection bin rather than mixing them with curbside items.
I carry a reusable tote to the store and skip taking paper or plastic bags for my purchases.
I collect used motor oil in a sealed container and deliver it to the auto parts store for recycling.
I put yard trimmings into the green cart and leave the lid closed until the collection day.
I sort glass by color when the drop-off center asks for clear, green, and brown separated.
I remove staples and plastic windows from junk mail before adding the paper to the recycling pile.
I empty aerosol cans completely and check with the city whether they belong in the metal recycling stream.
I fold clean aluminum foil into a ball and place it in the metals bin at the transfer station.
I track the pickup schedule on my calendar and set the recycling cart at the curb the night before.
